Saving some documents fails with a Postgres error. It happens when the text is
mostly unique tokens: hashes, IDs, base64, long tables of numbers. The document
search trigger caps its input at 1,000,000 characters, but Postgres's tsvector
size limit applies to the output, so a document under the cap can still produce
a search vector that's too big. The save errors out, the worker task that
refreshes the document text keeps retrying and failing, and the text and search
index go stale.

Saving such a document must succeed. When the full text produces a search
vector that is too large, index as much of the text as fits instead (at least
the beginning of the text). The title and the previous titles must still be
fully indexed, with their usual weights.

Saving these documents now works. When a document's full text would make a search vector too large, the search trigger indexes the longest beginning of the text that fits. The title and previous titles are always indexed in full, with their usual weights (A and C).

**The fix:** a new migration, `server/migrations/20261019120000-fit-document-search-vector-size.js`, which replaces `documents_search_trigger()`:
- It builds the title and previous-titles part of the vector first.
- It then tries the whole text (still capped at 1,000,000 characters). Most documents finish here, exactly as before.
- If Postgres reports the vector is too large, the trigger catches that error and binary-searches for the longest beginning of the text that fits next to the titles. It stops once the gap is under 1,000 characters, so it runs at most about 10 extra attempts, and only for these unusual documents.
- Each attempt includes the titles, so it checks the size of the final combined vector, not just the text part.

The text column itself is saved in full; only the search index is shortened. Because saving no longer fails, the worker task that refreshes the text stops retrying.
